title: The markdown parser renders #, ## and ### lines as headers
body:
`md::parse` in `src/md.rs` turns markdown into a `Vec<Block>`, where `Block` is `Paragraph`, `List`, `Code { lang, lines }` or `Table { header, rows }`. `md::layout` turns the blocks into ratatui lines for the screen, and `md::render` is the two together. A line that starts with `#`, `##` or `###` has no branch in `parse`. It joins the paragraph around it, and the screen shows the hashes as typed.

## Proposal

- A `Block::Heading { level: u8, text: Vec<Inline> }` variant. `parse` makes one from a line of one to three hashes, a space, and text. A heading closes the paragraph or list before it the way a blank line does.
- `layout` prints a heading bold, on its own line, with a blank line above it unless it is the first block.
- The CLI renderer proposed in the issue that this one blocks prints the same block, so headers come out the same on the screen and in `foam show`.
- `src/prime.rs` and the README list what foam renders. Both gain headers.

## Open

- Whether the three levels look different from each other on the screen, or all three render the same way. The screen has bold and colour to work with and little else.
- Whether four or more hashes stay literal text. I lean to yes, since nothing in foam wants that depth.
close_reason: Landed in commit f76d340, 'Render a line of one to three # as a heading'. The CLI side is foam-e14d0a.

notes.author: Jack Roddy/f1b5fba8
notes.text: Levels: one `#` is bold and underlined, two and three are bold and look the same. The screen has bold, dim, underline and colour, and a third distinct look did not seem worth a colour that means something else elsewhere. Four or more hashes, a bare hash, and a hash without a space stay text.
